name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated review of the last 500 tasks. This keeps the system self-correcting without manual checks. Trade-off: we accept slower updates for higher reliability—each change gets vetted before going live.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower updates—it’s that a fresh batch of 500 tasks could inherit the same flawed prompt before the review catches it. A better alternative: run the review *before* the change goes live, not after, so we catch regressions before they affect any tasks. Settle it by measuring how often the review catches critical errors in the last 500 tasks—if it’s under 90%, the loop is too slow to matter.
